title: What Does The Humble Birth Of Jesus Teach Us About Gods Character And His Ways
paragraphs: The Humble Birth of Jesus: Revealing God's Character and His Ways

Few events in human history are as striking and paradoxical as the birth of Jesus Christ. The King of kings, the eternal Son of God, entered the world not with royal fanfare, but in the humblest of circumstances—a manger, surrounded by animals, and welcomed by shepherds. This profound moment offers deep insights into the character of God and His ways with humanity.
1. God’s Humility and Approachability

The incarnation—God becoming flesh—exposes the remarkable humility of the Creator. Rather than choosing a palace or the halls of power, Jesus was born in a stable, affirming the truth later stated in Scripture:

Have this mind in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: who, existing in the form of God, counted not the being on an equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men. - Philippians 2:5-7 ASV

This humility reveals that God is not distant or unapproachable. He draws near to the lowly, meeting humanity in our need and brokenness. Jesus’ humble birth demonstrates that no one is too insignificant to receive God’s love.
2. God’s Rejection of Worldly Status

The world often values power, prestige, and wealth; but God’s ways confound human expectations. The choice of a poor, young woman (Mary) and a simple carpenter (Joseph) as Jesus’ earthly parents highlights God’s preference for the humble over the proud:
He hath put down princes from their thrones, and hath exalted them of low degree; the hungry he hath filled with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. - Luke 1:52-53 ASV
The humble birth of Jesus teaches us that God values faith, obedience, and humility over social status or wealth.
3. God’s Accessibility to All People
The announcement of Jesus’ birth came first to shepherds—people on the margins of society:
And the angel said unto them, Be not afraid; for behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy which shall be to all the people. - Luke 2:10 ASV

God’s message is not reserved for the elite or powerful but is for “all the people.” The birth of Jesus in such a humble setting demonstrates that the gospel is accessible to everyone, regardless of background or status.
4. God’s Faithfulness to His Promises
The location and circumstances of Jesus’ birth were not accidental, but the fulfillment of God’s promises through the prophets:
But thou, Bethlehem Ephrathah, which art little to be among the thousands of Judah, out of thee shall one come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel. - Micah 5:2 ASV
God’s sovereign plan works through the ordinary and the humble, reminding us that He is always faithful to keep His word, even in unexpected ways.
5. God’s Ultimate Purpose: Salvation by Grace

The humble birth points forward to Christ’s sacrificial death and resurrection. Jesus came “not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many” (Mark 10:45 ASV). His humility and obedience, even unto death, open the way of salvation for all who believe:
For by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God. - Ephesians 2:8 ASV
God’s ways overturn pride and self-reliance, calling us to humble trust in Christ alone.
Conclusion: Walking in the Humility of Christ

The birth of Jesus in humble circumstances is not only a revelation of God’s character but also an invitation to imitate Christ’s humility in our lives. As we celebrate the incarnation, we are called to reflect His character, serving others and trusting God’s wisdom—even when it looks different from the world’s expectations.
